title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Vinho Verde and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show Vinho Verde DOC, sometimes a sub-region like Monção e Melgaço or Lima, and often a grape: Alvarinho, Loureiro, Avesso. Regional wines may use Vinho Regional Minho. A sticker seal on the bottle certifies the DOC. Single-estate wines, from a quinta, are usually more serious than branded blends.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Vinho Verde suits light, fresh food: grilled sardines, clams, octopus, salads and sushi. Alvarinho suits richer seafood, bacalhau, grilled fish and white meat. Loureiro suits aperitifs and Asian food. Serve at 7 to 10 degrees. Most is best within a year; Alvarinho from Monção e Melgaço can age.

steps.prompt: Which dish suits a light Vinho Verde?
steps.explanation: Light, crisp wine suits simple grilled fish.

steps.body: In Portugal's summer festivals, grilled sardines and chilled Vinho Verde are a classic combination.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show the DOC, sub-region and often a grape
Vinho Verde suits sardines and seafood
Serve cold; most is best young
